passages.text: As they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage on the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent out two disciples, saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and at once you will find a donkey tied there, with her colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to Me.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was traveling with His disciples.
They came near Jerusalem.
They reached Bethphage.
Bethphage is on the Mount of Olives.
Jesus spoke to two of His disciples.
He sent them on a task.
He said, “Go into the village ahead of you.
You will find a donkey tied there.
Her colt will be with her.
Untie them.
Bring them to Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ εἰς τὸ ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν τότε Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς λέγων αὐτοῖς Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν καὶ εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετ’ αὐτῆς λύσαντες ἀγάγετέ μοι

passages.text: If anyone questions you, tell him that the Lord needs them, and he will send them right away.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His two disciples.
He gave them instructions.
He said, “If anyone asks you anything, answer him.
Say, ‘The Lord needs them.’
He will send the donkey and the colt immediately.”
passages.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ Κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει εὐθὺς δὲ ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς

passages.text: This took place to fulfill what was spoken through the prophet: “Say to the Daughter of Zion, ‘See, your King comes to you, gentle and riding on a donkey, on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’ ”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the King.
Jesus entered Jerusalem.
Jesus came in a gentle way.
Jesus rode on a donkey.
Jesus also rode on a colt, the young donkey.
God spoke about this event through a prophet long ago.
The prophet said, “Tell the people of Zion, ‘Look, your King is coming to you. He is gentle. He is riding on a donkey. He is riding on a colt, the foal of a donkey.’”
This happened to fulfill the prophet’s words.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών Ἰδοὺ ὁ Βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου

passages.text: So the disciples went and did as Jesus had directed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus was the teacher and leader of the disciples.
Jesus gave instructions to the disciples.
The disciples listened to Jesus.
The disciples went to do what Jesus told them.
The disciples did everything as Jesus directed.
passages.original: Πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς

passages.text: They brought the donkey and the colt and laid their cloaks on them, and Jesus sat on them.
passages.sermon: The disciples brought the donkey and the colt.\r\nThey placed their cloaks on the donkey and the colt.\r\nJesus sat on the cloaks.
passages.original: ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπ’ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν

passages.text: A massive crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
passages.sermon:
A large crowd gathered.
Many people took off their cloaks.
They spread their cloaks on the road.
Other people cut branches from the trees.
They spread the branches on the road.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ

passages.text: The crowds that went ahead of Him and those that followed were shouting: “Hosanna to the Son of David!” “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!” “Hosanna in the highest!”
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered Jerusalem.
Large crowds surrounded Jesus.
Some people walked ahead of Jesus.
Other people followed behind Jesus.
The crowds shouted loudly.
They said, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
They said, “Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!”
They said, “Hosanna in the highest!”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι Κυρίου Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις

passages.text: When Jesus had entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred and asked, “Who is this?”
passages.sermon: Jesus entered Jerusalem.\r\nThe whole city became stirred.\r\nThe people in the city asked, “Who is this?”
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος

passages.text: The crowds replied, “This is Jesus, the prophet from Nazareth in Galilee.”
passages.sermon:
The crowds spoke.
They said, “This is Jesus.”
Jesus is a prophet.
He comes from Nazareth.
Nazareth is in Galilee.
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας

passages.text: Then Jesus entered the temple courts and drove out all who were buying and selling there. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
passages.sermon:
Jesus entered the temple courts in Jerusalem.
He saw people buying and selling inside the temple.
He drove out everyone who was buying and selling there.
He overturned the tables of the money changers.
He overturned the seats of those who sold doves.
passages.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερόν καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς

passages.text: And He declared to them, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’ But you are making it ‘a den of robbers.’”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to the people in the temple.\r\nHe said, “It is written: ‘My house will be called a house of prayer.’”\r\nHe said, “You are making it a den of robbers.”
passages.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Γέγραπται Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ποιεῖτε Σπήλαιον λῃστῶν

passages.text: The blind and the lame came to Him at the temple, and He healed them.
passages.sermon:
Jesus stood in the temple.
Blind people came to Jesus in the temple.
Lame people came to Jesus in the temple.
Jesus healed the blind people.
Jesus healed the lame people.
passages.original: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς

passages.text: But the chief priests and scribes were indignant when they saw the wonders He performed and the children shouting in the temple courts, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the scribes saw Jesus.
They saw the wonderful things Jesus did.
They saw children in the temple courts.
The children shouted.
The children said, “Hosanna to the Son of David!”
The chief priests and the scribes became angry.
passages.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ ἠγανάκτησαν

passages.text: “Do you hear what these children are saying?” they asked. “Yes,” Jesus answered. “Have you never read: ‘From the mouths of children and infants You have ordained praise’?”
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and scribes spoke to Jesus.
They asked Him a question.
They said, “Do you hear what these children are saying?”
Jesus answered them.
He said, “Yes.”
Jesus continued speaking to them.
He said, “Have you never read this?”
He said, “‘From the mouths of children and infants, You have prepared praise.’”
passages.original: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς Ναί οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων Κατηρτίσω αἶνον

passages.text: Then He left them and went out of the city to Bethany, where He spent the night.
passages.sermon:
Jesus left the chief priests and scribes.
He went out of the city.
He went to Bethany.
He stayed there for the night.
passages.original: Καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ

passages.text: In the morning, as Jesus was returning to the city, He was hungry.
passages.sermon: Jesus was returning to the city in the morning.\r\nJesus felt hungry.
passages.original: Πρωῒ δὲ ἐπανάγων εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἐπείνασεν

passages.text: Seeing a fig tree by the road, He went up to it but found nothing on it except leaves. “May you never bear fruit again!” He said. And immediately the tree withered.
passages.sermon:
Jesus saw a fig tree by the road.
He went up to the fig tree.
He found nothing on the tree except leaves.
Jesus said to the tree, “May you never bear fruit again.”
The fig tree withered immediately.
passages.original: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν μίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἦλθεν ἐπ’ αὐτήν καὶ οὐδὲν εὗρεν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ φύλλα μόνον καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ Οὐ μηκέτι ἐκ σοῦ καρπὸς γένηται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα καὶ ἐξηράνθη παραχρῆμα ἡ συκῆ

passages.text: When the disciples saw this, they marveled and asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”
passages.sermon:
The disciples saw the fig tree.
They noticed it had withered immediately.
They were amazed.
They asked, “How did the fig tree wither so quickly?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες Πῶς παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη ἡ συκῆ

passages.text: “Truly I tell you,” Jesus replied, “if you have faith and do not doubt, not only will you do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to His disciples.
Jesus answered them.
He said, “Truly, I tell you this.
If you have faith, you can do great things.
If you do not doubt, you will have power.
You will not only do what happened to the fig tree.
You can do even greater things.
If you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.
Faith makes all things possible.”
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν καὶ μὴ διακριθῆτε οὐ μόνον τὸ τῆς συκῆς ποιήσετε ἀλλὰ κἂν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ εἴπητε Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν γενήσεται

passages.text: If you believe, you will receive whatever you ask for in prayer.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke to His disciples.\r\nJesus said, “If you believe, you will receive what you ask for in prayer.”
passages.original: καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ πιστεύοντες λήμψεσθε

passages.text: When Jesus returned to the temple courts and began to teach, the chief priests and elders of the people came up to Him. “By what authority are You doing these things?” they asked. “And who gave You this authority?”
passages.sermon:
Jesus returned to the temple courts.
Jesus began to teach there.
The chief priests and the elders of the people approached Jesus.
They spoke to Jesus.
They asked Jesus a question.
They said, “By what authority are you doing these things?”
They also asked, “Who gave you this authority?”
passages.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ διδάσκοντι οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ λέγοντες Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς καὶ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην

passages.text: “I will also ask you one question,” Jesus replied, “and if you answer Me, I will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests and elders.
He replied to their question.
He said, "I will ask you one question."
"If you answer Me,"
"I will tell you by what authority I do these things."
passages.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον ἕνα ὃν ἐὰν εἴπητέ μοι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν ἐρῶ ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ

passages.text: What was the source of John’s baptism? Was it from heaven or from men?” They deliberated among themselves and said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests and elders.
He asked them a question.
He said, “What was the source of John’s baptism?”
He asked, “Was it from heaven?”
He also asked, “Or was it from men?”
The chief priests and elders talked among themselves.
They said, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ He will ask us another question.”
They said, “He will ask, ‘Why then did you not believe John?’”
passages.original: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου πόθεν ἦν ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων Οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἐρεῖ ἡμῖν Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ

passages.text: But if we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people, for they all regard John as a prophet.”
passages.sermon:
The religious leaders spoke among themselves.
They considered what to say about John’s baptism.
They said, “If we say, ‘From men,’ we are afraid of the people.”
All the people believe John is a prophet.
The people honor John as a prophet.
The leaders fear the crowd because of this.
passages.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων φοβούμεθα τὸν ὄχλον πάντες γὰρ ὡς προφήτην ἔχουσιν τὸν Ἰωάννην

passages.text: So they answered, “We do not know.” And Jesus replied, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and elders spoke to Jesus.
They answered Jesus.
They said, “We do not know.”
Jesus replied to them.
He said, “I will not tell you by what authority I do these things.”
passages.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπαν Οὐκ οἴδαμεν Ἔφη αὐτοῖς καὶ αὐτός Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ

passages.text: But what do you think? There was a man who had two sons. He went to the first one and said, ‘Son, go and work today in the vineyard.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He wanted them to think about a situation.
He said, "What do you think?"
There was a man.
This man had two sons.
The man went to his first son.
He spoke to his first son.
He said, 'Son, go and work today in the vineyard.'
passages.original: Τί δὲ ὑμῖν δοκεῖ ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν τέκνα δύο καὶ προσελθὼν τῷ πρώτῳ εἶπεν Τέκνον ὕπαγε σήμερον ἐργάζου ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι

passages.text: ‘I will not,’ he replied. But later he changed his mind and went.
passages.sermon:
A man had two sons.
The man spoke to his first son.
The man said, “Son, go and work today in the vineyard.”
The first son answered his father.
He said, “I will not.”
Later, the first son changed his mind.
He went to work in the vineyard.
passages.original: Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Οὐ θέλω ὕστερον δὲ μεταμεληθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: Then the man went to the second son and told him the same thing. ‘I will, sir,’ he said. But he did not go.
passages.sermon:
A man had two sons.
He went to the second son.
He told the second son to go and work in the vineyard.
The second son answered, “I will, sir.”
But the second son did not go.
passages.original: Προσελθὼν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ εἶπεν ὡσαύτως Ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν Ἐγώ κύριε καὶ οὐκ ἀπῆλθεν

passages.text: Which of the two did the will of his father?” “The first,” they answered. Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, the tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a story about two sons.
He asked, "Which of the two sons did what his father wanted?"
The people answered, "The first son did."
Jesus replied to them.
He said, "I tell you the truth."
Tax collectors and prostitutes are entering the kingdom of God before you.
Jesus spoke these words to religious leaders.
The religious leaders did not obey God, even though they appeared righteous.
Tax collectors and prostitutes believed and obeyed God.
God welcomes those who truly repent and do His will.
passages.original: Τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐποίησεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός Λέγουσιν Ὁ πρῶτος Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι προάγουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For John came to you in a righteous way and you did not believe him, but the tax collectors and prostitutes did. And even after you saw this, you did not repent and believe him.
passages.sermon:
John came to you.
John lived in a righteous way.
You did not believe John.
Tax collectors believed John.
Prostitutes believed John.
You saw this.
You did not repent.
You did not believe John, even after seeing this.
passages.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ οἱ δὲ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐπίστευσαν αὐτῷ ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες οὐδὲ μετεμελήθητε ὕστερον τοῦ πιστεῦσαι αὐτῷ

passages.text: Listen to another parable: There was a landowner who planted a vineyard. He put a wall around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. Then he rented it out to some tenants and went away on a journey.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the people.
He told them a parable.
He said, "Listen to another parable."
There was a man who owned land.
He was a landowner.
He planted a vineyard on his land.
He put a wall around the vineyard.
He dug a winepress in the vineyard.
He built a tower in the vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to some tenants.
Then he went away on a journey.
passages.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἀκούσατε Ἄνθρωπος ἦν οἰκοδεσπότης ὅστις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ φραγμὸν αὐτῷ περιέθηκεν καὶ ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνὸν καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν

passages.text: When the harvest time drew near, he sent his servants to the tenants to collect his share of the fruit.
passages.sermon:
A landowner planted a vineyard.
He rented the vineyard to tenants.
He went away on a journey.
The time for harvest came close.
The landowner wanted his share of the fruit.
He sent his servants to the tenants.
He sent them to collect his share of the fruit.
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἤγγισεν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν καρπῶν ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς λαβεῖν τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτοῦ

passages.text: But the tenants seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned a third.
passages.sermon:
The tenants took the landowner’s servants.
They beat one servant.
They killed another servant.
They stoned a third servant.
passages.original: καὶ λαβόντες οἱ γεωργοὶ τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὃν μὲν ἔδειραν ὃν δὲ ἀπέκτειναν ὃν δὲ ἐλιθοβόλησαν

passages.text: Again, he sent other servants, more than the first group. But the tenants did the same to them.
passages.sermon:
The landowner sent more servants.
He sent more than the first group.
The tenants treated these servants the same way.
They harmed them as they did before.
passages.original: Πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους πλείονας τῶν πρώτων καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτοῖς ὡσαύτως

passages.text: Finally, he sent his son to them. ‘They will respect my son,’ he said.
passages.sermon: The owner of the vineyard sent his son to the tenants.\r\nHe sent his son after he had sent many servants.\r\nHe said, “They will respect my son.”
passages.original: Ὕστερον δὲ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου

passages.text: But when the tenants saw the son, they said to one another, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
passages.sermon:
The tenants worked in the vineyard.
They saw the son of the owner.
They spoke to each other.
They said, “This is the heir.”
They said, “Let us kill him.”
They said, “Then we will take his inheritance.”
passages.original: Οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἰδόντες τὸν υἱὸν εἶπον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτὸν καὶ σχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν αὐτοῦ

passages.text: So they seized him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
passages.sermon:
The tenants saw the son.
They seized him.
They threw him out of the vineyard.
They killed him.
passages.original: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος καὶ ἀπέκτειναν

passages.text: Therefore, when the owner of the vineyard returns, what will he do to those tenants?”
passages.sermon:
The owner controls the vineyard.
The tenants work in the vineyard.
The owner left the vineyard for a time.
The owner will return to the vineyard.
When the owner returns, he will see what the tenants have done.
What will the owner do to those tenants?
passages.original: Ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος τί ποιήσει τοῖς γεωργοῖς ἐκείνοις

passages.text: “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end,” they replied, “and will rent out the vineyard to other tenants who will give him his share of the fruit at harvest time.”
passages.sermon:
The people answered Jesus.
They said the owner will punish those wicked tenants.
He will destroy them completely.
He will give the vineyard to other tenants.
These new tenants will give the owner his share of the fruit at the proper time.
passages.original: Λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐκδώσεται ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς οἵτινες ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρποὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς αὐτῶν

passages.text: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This is from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to them.
Jesus is the Son of God.
He asked them a question.
He said, "Have you never read the Scriptures?"
The Scriptures are the holy writings of God.
He quoted the Scriptures.
He said, "The builders rejected a stone."
The builders are those who lead and build.
They did not accept the stone.
That stone became the cornerstone.
The cornerstone is the most important stone in a building.
The Lord made this happen.
This work is marvelous to us.
We see it and wonder at it.
passages.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες Οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας Παρὰ Κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη Καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν

passages.text: Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a people who will produce its fruit.
passages.sermon:
Jesus spoke to the chief priests and Pharisees.
He said, “God will take away the kingdom of God from you.
God will give the kingdom to another people.
These people will produce the fruit of the kingdom.”
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς

passages.text: He who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces, but he on whom it falls will be crushed.”
passages.sermon: Jesus spoke about himself as the cornerstone.\r\nHe said, “Anyone who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces.\r\nIf this stone falls on someone, it will crush that person.”
passages.original: καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται ἐφ’ ὃν δ’ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν

passages.text: When the chief priests and Pharisees heard His parables, they knew that Jesus was speaking about them.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests heard the parables of Jesus.
The Pharisees also heard the parables of Jesus.
They understood the meaning of the parables.
They knew that Jesus was speaking about them.
passages.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει

passages.text: Although they wanted to arrest Him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the people regarded Him as a prophet.
passages.sermon:
The chief priests and the Pharisees wanted to arrest Jesus.
They did not arrest Him.
They feared the crowds.
The people regarded Jesus as a prophet.
passages.original: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους ἐπεὶ εἰς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον
